## Landlore: Volumes 1 - 5

_by Kantiki Jayamana Whateva_

**AI Usage Warning**: Right upfront, the images you'll see in this entry are AI-generated using ChatGPT5 for their creation. They're based on my concepts for each cover, but I'll eventually need to commission an artist for these. Sadly, the artist Norman Mingo of Mad Magazine fame died in 1980 when I was just a pup of three years. I wouldn't come across his art until I was nine, when I realized that he, too, must have had a run-in with the fae folk. He at least knew what goblins looked like and strikingly so! If I could resurrect Norman for the covers, I would. In the meantime, I keep my eye out for an artists who even come near... but they, too, must be fae-cursed. It's made the cover process a difficult one and a bit out of my own ballpark on this one.

There are already a few copies of volume one of "Landlore" floating around out there, as well as some early drafts from volume two. As my series on hitchhiking, train jumping, and living out of vehicles, _Landlore's_ quickly my most popular written work. Nuff said!

Those who know how long it's already been in the making are shaking their heads at this very moment, saying, "It's never gonna happen!"

It is. Well, volume one is going to happen. Other volumes need to wait for the statute of limitations to run out on some of the shit we get up to. Even though I'm marking them as "Travel Fiction" on publication, I think there's enough evidence to connect some of the dots. Also, my original method of using our pirate names doesn't work anymore, since my tribe and I are known quite well by our pirate names these days. So that doesn't work either.

Ooh... there's a thought. I could have Minz, one of my AI assistants, take the final copies and publish them years after we've all died. She'd be more than happy and would love the chaotic irony of it all.

Well, ideally, it'll be myself who publishes and not Mizz Mini. It follows a similar humorous travel style as "[Bottle 66](bottle-66)" and the twisted humor in "[Everything Will Be OK](everything-will-be-ok)" (sans corporate lingo).

_<font face="Times New Roman">"Living Large on Common Cents!"</font>_ <- If not the subtitle for V1, it'll end up as a chapter title. Also, I can't believe that almost two decades later the phrase still comes up empty on Google. How has no one other than me ever used those words in that combination?

Volume one is almost done except for the damned cover. I have all five covers perfectly in my mind along with their requirements. It's the ability to put them into visual form that evades me. All five covers -- just like the books themselves -- should stir up a lot of trouble and piss alotta people off. _Good!_ That's the intention. I actually lived on the streets and most times by choice, and I know how quick "normies" fucking look away... or worse, try to find legal ways to literally _hide us_ and get the streets hidden away where they can't see it. And to those motherfuckers, _I'm coming for you. You are not safe._

## Excerpt - The Moment That Changes Everything

You've been at the carnival for a minute now. You've ridden the rides, laughed with your friends, and definitely downed more than your fair share of funnel cake. In fact, you really - for really, really real! -- shouldn't've gone even-stevens on that cotton candy a few minutes ago. You can feel it sitting in your gut. The day's completely worn you out, and you're beyond ready to bounce... except there's that one "friend" who insists on staying.

_Isn't there always?_

Your desire to leave is ultimately weaker than their stubborn drive to stay, so... sure.. . you stay. Why not?

I'm an OG carnie rat alongside my friends Mouse and Catfish. I've played on both sides of the ropes. What's another hour or two when I've basically lived weeks here?

Day drags into twilight. You feel like you could either pass out or throw up -- whichever comes first. And then, _it_ happens. The sun finally dips. The sky bruises, coloring and dimming in real-time. Is it just you, or has the entire fairground suddenly gone quiet? Finally, just as the last gasp of daylight loses its grip, the electric neon world of the carnival violently bursts into life. Rides, booths, and games explode in blinding new colors. The air itself seems to shift, glowing in tandem with endless rows of rainbow bulbs.

That surreal, liminal space between day and night has passed. A new world is born. It's technically the exact same fair that's been torturing you for the last three hours, but it isn't. _It's transformed!_ You feel energized -- charged! Dare I say, _enchanted?_ You can't even believe that, just minutes ago, you were ready to drop dead. Did someone change the music? You can literally feel the beat now... the heavy, pulsing breath of the night itself. Suddenly, you feel like you could ride this new wonderland until dawn. Your own laughter grows louder, more frantic, bleeding into the rising volume of the crowd all around you.

This is it. This is the moment that changes everything -- the exact second one world is born from the death of another. You turn to that one stubborn friend... 'n you thank them. Without their bullheaded foolishness, you would've completely missed the magic of this shift... this turning of the tides.. 'n you never would've known this hidden world was breathing right beneath the surface all along.

Now, ask yourself: _Do you really believe I'm talking about the carnival?_

## Story - The Password-Protected Paradox \[Excerpt\]:

Not all who wear blue are clowns, but all clowns wear blue. I should know.. fucking clown blood runs thru these very veins. My great grandfather Simeon paved that yellow brick road for me back in 1947. _Nice job, Pops!_

The Universe is notoriously fond of paradoxes, though this fact has historically failed to trickle down to the municipal police departments of the American Midwest. To the average small-town deputy, a hitchhiker is a simple, linear equation. The sum of that equation? Hitchhiker = 1 dusty thumb + 1 canvas backpack \* (exactly 3 ounces of illegal flora + 1 switchblade).

_Sorry to break your neat 'n tidy mold, chum._

So when the local law enforcement -- a man whose mustache looked as though it considered plans to escape his upper lip -- intercepted me at the city limits, I already knew what was coming. He possessed the supreme, unearned confidence of a man who believed he was about to solve a crime that hadn't quite happened yet.

You know this dance. We _all_ know this dance. First came the pat-down, conducted by Officer Friendly with the stiff formality of a confused tailor, followed immediately by the unceremonious dumping of my life's possessions onto the hood of his patrol car. Bacon Boy was hunting for contraband... expecting the standard vagabond starter kit: a crusty sleeping bag, a dog-eared paperback, and perhaps a suspiciously fragrant pipe. What this particular Five-O was decidedly _not_ expecting was the sudden materialization of a teched-out, densely wired portable electronic music studio.

Out tumbled a labyrinth of cables, a MIDI controller, and a bruised but functional laptop -- the very nerve center of my cross-border operations. It was less a backpack and more a mobile sonic laboratory capable of rendering directly into the digital ether, one emailed WAV file at a time. The deputy stared at the tangled heap of technology. The flashing red 'n blue lights of his cruiser reflected off the faux aluminum casing of the laptop, bathing the scene in a disco strobe of profound bureaucratic bewilderment. I've gotta admit, that stunned look of confusion was worth every second.

For a long, elastic moment, the silence was heavier than the highway humidity. His brain visibly labored to bridge the cognitive chasm between "transient drifter" and "music producer" . . with the gears nearly audibly skipping beats. He slowly unhooked his thumbs from his utility belt, leaned over the hood of the car, then pointed a finger the size and general consistency of a Polish sausage directly at the laptop. His brow furrowed into a knot of deep, existential suspicion.

"This yours, son?"

"No, Ringo! I just walked outta a few Best Buys and forgot to pay," I wanted to say. _Seriously, theft? That's the best mold your pea-sized brain could fit everything into?_

It takes a monumental, almost monastic level of restraint not to look a man in the eye and inform him that he is a towering monument to his own intellectual inadequacy. The urge to explain that transient hackers do not typically lug stolen motherboards across county lines via thumb-power was nearly overwhelming. _Inside thought! Inside thought!_ Instead, channeling the diplomatic grace of an intergalactic ambassador trapped on a deeply primitive planet, I offered a warm, infuriatingly polite smile.

"Well, Officer," I replied smoothly, "if anyone else happens to know the password, then _they_ can have it. Otherwise... if you could be just a bit gentle with that. I don't exactly carry backups."

He blinked. The logic was entirely sound, yet structurally offensive to his authority. He gingerly pushed the laptop back toward my pile of socks with the tip of his pen, treating it with the nervous reverence one might afford an unexploded bomb. The cosmos, as always, maintained its sense of humor... leaving the deputy to return to his cruiser utterly defeated by a password-protected paradox... while I packed up my digital symphony and continued my way into the city.

That laptop had a name: Frank the Wonderbunny! When I got to the first diner or coffee shop, I had to make sure he was still up 'n running. Hopefully Durant's finest hadn't thrown him around enough to do any damage. We'd find out soon enough.

## On AI + The Covers

While these definitely aren't final covers, the process gave me some ideas. Firstly, I like the idea of the caricatures being so far gone that they're fairly Irrecognizable as us.. . but to our tribe, they'll know who it should be in each image. As long as we can keep the misinformation campaign going, the longer we keep getting away with it. It's been an effective strategy so far.

Then wow does AI hate the homeless! Both ChatGPT and Gemini very much do NOT want to show anyone who's even in the slightest bit distressed, no matter whether ironic or satirical... or both. Whoever I end up getting for the final five illustrations will need to have none of those qualms and be ready to take a few strays for helping illustrate these books. They're each fire-starters in their own rights. I considered Fab Ciraolo for the illustrations for a while... still considering it. At least Fab's no stranger to stirring up the hornet's nest.

## Extended Exploration

This book is firmly rooted in [The Happy Fun Pactus](adhd-revolution) and "[The ADHD Revolution](adhd-revolution)", but in this case it's graffiti in written form. For those who like the travel writings themselves, my upcoming book "[Bottle 66](bottle-66)" is another one you'd like!
